title: Add benchmark-lab profiling baselines and reporting pipeline v68
author: Riley Chen
release_notes: Add updated profiling baselines and reporting pipeline v68; improves memory accounting for mixed workloads and adds new CSV exports for cost analysis.
description: Context: The benchmark lab needs updated profiling baselines for representative mixed workloads and a more robust reporting pipeline to export per-run cost/memory breakdowns and enable longitudinal comparisons. This PR introduces profiling baselines v68, a CSV/Parquet reporting exporter, a lightweight benchmark smoke CI workflow, and a small but critical memory-accounting fix for KV cache warmup. Motivation: recent model variants with longer context lengths exposed underestimated peak memory usage in our profiling artifacts, which caused misleading cost projections for Dedicated capacity planning. This change corrects the accounting and provides richer reporting to support cost analysis and SLA planning. Changes included (high level):  - Add 13 new baseline definitions under benchmark-lab/baselines/v68 covering short/med/long contexts and mixed token-generation workloads.  - Fix memory accounting in runner/kvcache.py: include cold-KV warmup allocations in peak working set measurement.  - Add reporting/csv_exporter.py and reporting/parquet_uploader.py to emit per-run token/cost/memory breakdowns and upload to S3 for downstream dashboards.  - Add CI workflow ci/workflows/benchmark-smoke.yml that runs a fast subset of representative runners on a single GPU in staging.  - Documentation: update docs/benchmark-lab/README.md with baseline definitions and migration steps. Checklist: - [x] Baselines reviewed and validated on staging (gpu-pool-staging) - [x] Memory accounting unit tests added and green - [x] Reporting exporter tested against sample runs and S3 staging - [x] CI smoke workflow configured with secrets masked - [x] Release notes drafted This PR is intentionally scoped to avoid changes to the core serving runtime; only benchmark lab artifacts and tooling are affected. Migration notes: after merge, run scripts/migrations/upgrade_baselines.py in benchmark-lab namespace to register v68 baselines and re-run a full profiling sweep to populate the new reporting tables. Testing & results: ran full staging benchmark sweep across 8 models and observed: - Median latency change across workloads: +0.9% (within noise) - Peak memory for long-context runs: -12% (due to accounting fix surfacing previously hidden allocations and adjustments to batching heuristics) - CSV exporter produced per-run cost breakdowns; sample CSV uploaded to s3://redwood-benchmark-staging/v68-samples/ Rollout: merge to main, deploy benchmark-lab CI runner image (tag v68), register baselines, then schedule a full profiling job. Related: ENG-3124, ENG-3189. If issues are observed, revert the reporting exporter independently (no runtime changes) and re-run the baseline migration to previous artifacts.
